source.title: Responding to the emotions of others: dissociating forms of empathy through the study of typical and psychiatric populations

confidence_rationale: Canonical, widely-replicated clinical dissociation providing the strongest real-world existence proof that concern-relevant social competence and affective empathy come apart: in psychopathy, cognitive empathy (Theory of Mind) and motor empathy are intact while a SPECIFIC form of emotional empathy is impaired. This is precisely the configuration Q-091 fears in an artificial system -- fluent, structurally competent social output over a missing affective-relevance component. Source quality is high (NIMH review, heavily cited, mechanistically grounded). Confidence held below 0.8 because the dissociation Blair documents is between cognitive-ToM and affective empathy, not specifically between LINGUISTIC FLUENCY and affective empathy; the psychopathy case is an analogy for the masking risk, not a direct measurement of a fluent language system masking absent empathy.
failure_signatures: Blair explicitly argues empathy is NOT a unitary system but a loose collection of partially dissociable neurocognitive systems -- so a single behavioural readout (e.g. concern-shaped language) cannot certify that all component systems are present and functioning.

In psychopathy the impaired component is a specific form of EMOTIONAL empathy while cognitive and motor empathy are intact -- i.e. the population that most convincingly presents concern-shaped social behaviour is exactly the one missing the affective-relevance architecture, the masking hazard made concrete.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Empathy is not a unitary function but three partially dissociable systems -- cognitive empathy (Theory of Mind), motor empathy, and emotional empathy. Individuals with psychopathy show clear difficulties with a specific form of emotional empathy but no indications of impairment with cognitive and motor empathy; individuals with autism show the converse profile.
mapping.ree_translation: The dissociability of empathy sub-systems in humans is the biological warrant for Q-091's worry: because a socially-competent-looking output (intact cognitive/ToM empathy) can be produced while a distinct affective component is absent (psychopathy), an evaluator who reads competent social output as proof of the whole empathy stack will be systematically fooled. In REE terms, the ARC-123/MECH-405 separation means a language channel can be fluent and concern-shaped while the other-model + affective-relevance architecture (the thing caring commitment actually requires) is immature or absent -- so evaluation must probe the affective/other-directed component directly, not infer it from social-linguistic fluency.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a human clinical dissociation between cognitive-ToM empathy and affective empathy, NOT a demonstration that linguistic fluency specifically masks affective empathy, and not a demonstration in any artificial system. Psychopaths' intact 'cognitive empathy' is not the same construct as a language model's fluency, and the transfer to a not-yet-built REE V4 substrate is an analogy about architecture, not a measured effect.
mapping.source_context: Selective review of the human empathy literature drawing on typical development and two psychiatric populations (autism, psychopathy); cognitive-neuroscience framing.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (canonical review, robust clinical dissociation). Mapping fidelity moderate: it evidences dissociability of empathy components generally, which underwrites the masking premise, but the specific axis Q-091 names (linguistic fluency vs affective empathy) is one step removed from the cognitive-ToM vs emotional-empathy axis Blair measures. Transfer risk elevated by human-clinical -> artificial-substrate extrapolation.
